newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-RONALDO SCORES HAT TRICK AS BRAZIL BEAT LITHUANIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RONALDO SCORES HAT TRICK AS BRAZIL BEAT LITHUANIA.

text.p: Striker Ronaldo, who has made a spectacular start to the season with Spanish club Barcelona, scored a hat trick as world champions Brazil beat Lithuania 3-1 in a friendly soccer international on Wednesday.
The 20-year-old has been compared to a host of stars from the past since joining the Catalan giants from Dutch side PSV Eindhoven.
On Wednesday he went on another scoring spree, this time for his country, who are a building a side to defend the World Cup in France in 1998.
Ronaldo's mere presence appeared to unnerve the Lithuanian defence and he had two penalty appeals turned down before notching his first goal in the 14th minute.

Midfielder Djalminha, making his international debut, split the defence with a crossfield pass and Ronaldo controlled the ball with his chest before flicking it past goalkeeper Valdemaras Martinkenas.

Ronaldo scored his second from close range on the stroke of halftime after the Lithuanian defence missed another cross by Djalminha. He completed his hat-trick in the 70th minute after another blunder by the East European rearguard.
Defender Naglis Miknevicius underhit a pass back to the goalkeeper and Ronaldo intercepted the ball and beat off a challenge by two defenders to score again.
Lithuania's Buitkus had put his team back on level terms in the 21st minute with a rasping drive from 30 meters.

Brazil, with Leonardo and Mauro Silva the only survivors from the 1994 World Cup team, were inspired by the trickery of Djalminha and the intelligent play of Leonardo in midfield but their defence looked shaky.

Brazil defender Andre Cruz was sent off in the last minute but should have been dismissed 20 minutes earlier for a horrendous challenge on an opponent. He had already been booked but was amazingly allowed to stay on the field.

Lithuania made seven changes from the side which started last week's World Cup qualifying match against Liechtenstein with star striker Ariminas Narbekovas, who plays for Austrian club Admira Wacker, among the absentees.

Despite suffering in the high temperatures, which hovered around 30 C at kickoff time at nine o'clock in the evening, they produced some deft touches in midfield but were let down by wreckless defending.

Despite a 60,000 crowd, the match was spoiled by the poor surface. The ball bounced around as if the game was being played on a dirt pitch on a piece of waste ground, while the second half was delayed for 20 minutes by a floodlight failure.

Brazil - 1-Zetti, 2-Ze Maria, 3-Goncalves, 4-Andre Cruz, 6- Andre Luis (16-Ze Roberto, 46th minute), 5-Mauro Silva, 8-Flavio Conceicao, 10-Leonardo, 11-Djalminha, 7-Donizete (20-Edmundo, 46th), 9-Ronaldo

Lithuania - 1-Valdemaras Martinkenas, 5-Raimondas Vainoras, 4-Naglis Miknevicius, 3-Darius Gvildys (16-Giderius Zhutautas), 6-Poderis (14-Morinas), 8-Buitkus, 2-Sorolainus, 9-Raimondas Zhutautas, 10-Igoris Kirilovas (15-Tomas Razanauskas, 73rd), 11- Preiksaitis, 7-Darius Maciulevicius.
